title: Hanne B NDE 3426
content: When I was three years old I fell out of an open window from the fourth floor. I remember the fall; remember lying on my back on the concrete tiles, looking up at the open window above and then my mother and aunt rushing towards me screaming loudly with their outstretched arms. Then a 'gap'. Next I found 'myself zooming out', seeing the backs of my mother, aunt and many people I did not know leaning over a little 'empty shell'. There was a square white 'box' with two lamps shining on this (must have been an ambulance, but I had never seen one). The 'scene' disappeared as I was zooming out and up, the rooftops and chimneys went out of sight, and the next 'thing' I remember (vividly!) is that I was between thousands of stars and spiraling galaxies they were All Around 'me' and I was part of the Whole. (I did not know back then, what a galaxy was, let alone a spiraling one.) I felt One and All Consciousness and extremely happy. The night sky around me was the most beautiful Royal Blue and I was 'clad' in a 'floating garment' with a long, pointed hat on my 'head', which was pure light. When I moved my 'hands', stars would spring from them and join the rest on the firmament. As I was too young to know what a 'magician' would look like I had no idea - but how I loved it all! When I grew older, I could read about 'magicians' and wondered. The 'Hubble Telescope' and many other sources filled me in on the spiraling galaxies later on in life: Home Again. Have to add that when I found myself strapped tightly into a narrow little bed in hospital and the nurses/doctors treated me as a little kid (they can be forgiven :-) ) that I thought: If you just knew how old I really am. And 'waking up' was much less thrilling than my NDE experience, trust that. For some reason I felt that I should not tell anyone about my 'extraterrestrial experience', this including my beloved mother, because she might be worried. I told her many years later when I was a teenager, this when she told me that I had been declared stone dead by the doctors - and that when I came to, they had told her that I would be brainless. Well, it was not so, and she blamed them for having been so cruel. That is when I found it fair to tell her of my beautiful experience. Fair on her - and fair on the doctors. She was utmost surprised; this is put mildly, and kept asking me for more. How she deserved it, poor mum. But time had to be ripe, for both of us, and we decided to keep it between us. As the decennia went by, many more people turned out to have had amazing experiences when 'dead', and I think it is of utmost importance for so many people being so scared of death to know, that 'this dimension' is NOT 'all there is'. That we are multi-dimensional beings. If that was not so - 'who' was the 'being' flying between the galaxies and 'who' was the three year old who 'woke up'? If anything, I 'woke down'. :-)
